def kth_largest(nums: list[int], k: int) -> int:
    """
    Find the k-th largest element in an unsorted list using a Max-Heap approach.
    The time complexity for building the heap is O(n) and for extracting k elements 
    is O(k log n), resulting in an overall average and worst-case time complexity of O(n + k log n).
    """
    import heapq

    if k < 1 or k > len(nums):
        return None
    
    # Convert nums into a max-heap by inverting the values
    max_heap = [-num for num in nums]
    heapq.heapify(max_heap)
    
    # Extract the largest k times
    for _ in range(k):
        kth_largest = -heapq.heappop(max_heap)
    
    return kth_largest

def kth_largest(nums: list[int], k: int) -> int:
    """
    Find the k-th largest element in an unsorted list using the Min-Heap approach.
    The time complexity for building the heap is O(n) and maintaining the heap 
    to keep the k largest elements is O(k log n), resulting in an overall 
    time complexity of O(n + k log n).
    """
    import heapq

    if k < 1 or k > len(nums):
        return None

    # Create a min-heap for the k largest elements
    min_heap = []
    
    for num in nums:
        heapq.heappush(min_heap, num)
        if len(min_heap) > k:
            heapq.heappop(min_heap)
    
    return min_heap[0]  # The root of the min-heap is the k-th largest element
